Research, Success and KATİP scholarships run on separate periods.
official.application_cycle: Annual general application window, 10 January - 20 February (2026 cycle closed; next window expected to open 10 January 2027)
official.status_note: The 2026 application period ran 10 January - 20 February 2026 and is now closed; the programme's published calendar repeats the 10 January - 20 February window annually, so the next general window is expected in January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'Covers tuition fees' and 'While studying at the most prestigious universities at world standards, your university tuition is covered by Türkiye Scholarships.'
benefits: Monthly stipend 6.500 TL at associate and bachelor's level, 9.500 TL at master's level and 13.000 TL at PhD level
Merit Scholarship Program awardees receive a monthly stipend twice the regular amount
Tuition fee covered at the host university in Türkiye

Dormitory accommodation with fees covered (undergraduate level for the duration of studies; graduate students in the first year), or a housing allowance of 6.000 TL for Istanbul and Ankara and 5.000 TL for other cities for graduate students renting after the first year

Once-off flight ticket at the beginning of education and when graduating, a 1-year free Turkish language course (TÖMER), university and department placement, and social and cultural activities including the International Student Academy
eligibility: Graduates or those who will graduate at the end of the current academic year (before August)
Turkish citizens and individuals who have lost Turkish citizenship are ineligible
Individuals who are currently enrolled in programs in Turkish universities at the level of education they will apply for are ineligible
requirements: Minimum academic achievement: 70% for associate and bachelor's degree candidates; 75% for graduate candidates; 90% for candidates of Health Sciences (Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy)
Age criteria: under 21 for associate and bachelor's programmes; under 30 for master's; under 35 for PhD; under 50 for Research Scholarship
Türkiye Scholarships does not award scholarships in the field of health sciences at graduate level

Candidates wishing to study in English or other language-medium programmes must provide an internationally accepted language proficiency certificate (TOEFL or other equivalent certifications if officially stated acceptable by the university)
All awardees who do not possess a C1 Level Certificate for Turkish Proficiency must attend the 1-year Turkish Language Course and attain the C1 Level Certificate by the end of their academic year

Undergraduate candidates holding international qualifications such as SAT or GCSE instead of national exam scores must provide the minimum required qualifications for completing secondary school according to these international exams
documents: A valid identity document, ID card or passport, and a photograph of the candidate taken within the last 1 year
International exam results (GRE, GMAT, SAT, etc.) and international language test results (TOEFL, DELF, etc.) if required by the chosen university or program

A proposal for a research topic and a written example of the research carried out (only for PhD applications; candidates invited to interview must also bring the originals of all documents of the latest education completed)
selection_criteria: Applications are considered according to the candidate's academic success, social activities and motivation related to the chosen field
Preliminary assessment on basic criteria: minimum academic achievement, age limits set for each level of education, and required documents

Expert evaluation by the Expert Committee of academic status, previous qualifications, academic interests, career goals, consistency of preferences, content of the letter of intent, and participation in social activities

A 30-question quantitative test (mathematics, geometry and logic, 60 minutes) is held for undergraduate candidates prior to the face-to-face interviews, with results compared within the applicant's field
Face-to-face interview of usually 15-30 minutes conducted by interview committees of academics and experts
Final assessment by a selection committee, which evaluates the general eligibility of the candidate
coverage: Turkish Language Course (1 Year) and University and Department Placement
application_method: Free online application through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS)
Register in TBBS, upload the required documents, select up to 12 choices in the online application, and submit
official.application_route: Apply free of charge online through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS) during the single annual window; successful candidates are placed in universities and departments by Türkiye Scholarships
official.study_mode: Full-time degree programmes; short-term (research) programmes run under separate application periods
official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens of all countries; Turkish citizens and individuals who have lost Turkish citizenship are ineligible
official.international_eligibility: Türkiye Scholarships applications are open to international students from all countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Türkiye Scholarships does not award scholarships in the field of health sciences at graduate level; the Art Scholarship Program is limited to specified music, performing arts and fine arts departments at Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University and İstanbul Technical University
official.research_requirement: PhD applications must include a proposal for a research topic and a written example of the research carried out
official.duration: Full-time degree programmes at associate (two-year technical and vocational education and training), bachelor's, master's and PhD levels, including a 1-year Turkish language course for awardees without C1 Turkish proficiency
official.description: Türkiye Scholarships is a government-funded, competitive scholarship program awarded to outstanding students and researchers to pursue full-time or short-term programs at the top universities in Türkiye, aiming to build a network of future leaders committed to strengthening cooperation among countries and mutual understanding among societies. Beyond financial support it provides university and department placement, tuition fees, accommodation, health insurance, a monthly stipend, a once-off flight ticket, a 1-year Turkish language course and academic, social and cultural facilities. Applications for associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees are received in one annual period, 10 January - 20 February.
official.program_type: Government scholarship programme of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB)
official.english_requirement: No blanket English requirement for the general scholarship: candidates who wish to study in English-medium programmes must provide an internationally accepted language proficiency certificate (TOEFL or other equivalent as officially stated acceptable by the university). The Merit Scholarship Program requires TOEFL IBT 80/120 or IELTS 6.5/9.0 at undergraduate level and TOEFL IBT 90/120 or IELTS 7.0/9.0 at master's and PhD levels.

verification.notes: All amounts, benefits, criteria, documents and process details were taken from the official turkiyeburslari.gov.tr pages (YTB); stipend figures (6.500/9.500/13.000 TL) were read on the 'Why Türkiye Scholarships?' and 'Full-Time Scholarships' pages, documents and language rules on 'Application in 5 Steps', selection stages on 'Evaluation and Selection Process', and the annual calendar on 'Application Calendar'.

applicant_utility.summary: Türkiye Scholarships funds the whole package - tuition, dormitory, health insurance, a top-up housing allowance for graduate students, flight tickets and a sizeable monthly stipend (6.500 TL undergraduate, 9.500 TL master's, 13.000 TL PhD) - but you apply for the scholarship, not to a university: you rank up to 12 choices and YTB assigns the institution and department. The 2026 round closed on 20 February 2026, so treat the next 10 January 2027 window as your target and prepare documents in autumn 2026. Expect a roughly six-month decision cycle: documentary screening March-April, a 30-question quantitative test plus in-person interview April-June for many candidates, results in early August and arrival in September. Because Turkish is the language of most departments and awardees must reach C1, plan your first year around the compulsory one-year Turkish course even if your programme is taught in English.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong all-round students from any country who want a fully funded degree in Türkiye, meet their level's grade and age cut-offs, and accept that YTB rather than the applicant chooses the university and department.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you will hold the diploma or a temporary graduation certificate before the February deadline, and that your transcripts show 70% (or 75%/90% at graduate/health level)
Check the language of instruction and any GRE, GMAT, SAT or TOEFL requirement of every programme you plan to rank in TBBS before you submit your 12 choices
Draft the PhD research topic proposal and written sample of completed research early - they are mandatory uploads, not attachments you can add later
Get a passport-style photo taken within the last year and scan your passport or ID card and transcripts at readable resolution
Register in TBBS ahead of the January rush, save your credentials, and download the cycle announcement and calendar page for reference
Read the Merit Scholarship thresholds if you are targeting a doubled stipend (GWA 90%, plus the listed exam and language scores)
common_rejection_risks: Failing the preliminary assessment on missing or illegible diploma, transcript or identity documents - the first screen is purely documentary
Sitting below the level-specific minimum grade (70% undergraduate, 75% graduate, 90% health sciences) or over the age cap (under 21/30/35)
Being an ineligible case without realising it: current Turkish citizenship or a former Turkish citizen, or already enrolled at a Turkish university at the level applied for
Ranking English-medium programmes without the TOEFL or GRE/GMAT/SAT scores that the specific university demands
Preference list that is inconsistent with your academic background or a thin letter of intent - expert evaluation explicitly scores consistency of preferences and motivation
PhD applicants omitting the research proposal and written research sample
Undergraduate candidates underestimating the 60-minute, 30-question quantitative test drawn from Turkish curriculum core topics
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa fees, any costs of obtaining GRE/GMAT/SAT/TOEFL certificates, personal spending beyond the monthly stipend, and for master's and PhD students after the first dormitory year, any rent shortfall above the published housing allowance of 6.000 TL (Istanbul and Ankara) or 5.000 TL (other cities).
document_audit: Names and birth dates on the passport/ID must match the diploma and transcript exactly - mismatches are a standard first-screen rejection
The photo must be taken within the last 1 year; an older photograph is rejected
National exam results are optional to upload, but omitting them weakens the academic record; holders of SAT or GCSE must evidence secondary-school completion minimums
The research proposal and research sample are separate PhD upload slots - one file cannot serve for both
Shortlisted candidates must carry originals of their most recent education documents to the interview; unverifiable certificates collapse the file at the interview stage
alerts: The application window is fixed and short - 10 January to 20 February - with no rolling or late admissions, so missing it costs a full year
One annual round only for degree study; Research Scholarships (four periods), Success Scholarships (October-November) and KATİP have their own calendars
Results arrive in early August for September arrival, so do not rely on this programme as a same-year back-up after other deadlines close
The quantitative test is described as written for the Turkish curriculum core and questions are provided in Turkish and English - brush up on Turkish secondary mathematics, geometry and logic
The C1 Turkish requirement continues after arrival: awardees without a C1 certificate must attend the year-long course and attain C1 by the end of the academic year
Graduate accommodation support covers only the first dormitory year, so budget for renting from year two
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on TBBS, complete the form, upload all documents, rank up to 12 choices and submit by 20 February; screening runs March-April, test and interviews April-June, results land in early August.
